quality.notes: CRF 18 = high quality (~15-20 MB/min). Lower = better quality but larger files.
quality.notes_jpeg: JPEG quality 90 for sharper text. Default is 80.

resolution.notes: 1080p30 is optimal for YouTube. 4K only if content demands it (slower render).

encoding.notes: slow preset = better compression (smaller file, same quality). medium = faster render.
encoding.notes_two_pass: CRF mode is generally better than 2-pass for YouTube.

performance.benchmark: Run `npx remotion benchmark` to find optimal concurrency
performance.gpu_effects: Avoid WebGL/canvas effects in cloud (no GPU). Use precomputed images instead.
performance.memoization: Use useMemo() and useCallback() in React components for expensive computation

draft.notes: Fast render, lower quality. Good for review cycles.

standard.notes: Good balance of quality and file size.

high.notes: Best quality for YouTube. Our default setting.

maximum.notes: Largest files. Only for special cases.

youtube_optimization.file_size_target: Under 128GB (YouTube limit), aim for under 100MB per minute
notes: H.264 is most compatible with YouTube's processing
H.265/HEVC is 50% smaller but not universally supported
VP9 is open source but very slow to encode
CRF 18-20 is the sweet spot for YouTube quality

performance_tips: Use <Video> from @remotion/media for best rendering performance
Avoid WebGL/canvas effects in cloud (no GPU)
Use useMemo() and useCallback() for expensive computation
Run `npx remotion benchmark` to find optimal concurrency
PNG format is slower than JPEG — only use for transparent video
Higher resolution = slower render. Scale down with --scale if needed
